summary: Big Bend lookout, Wythe County VA: CCC-built 1941, bought and taken down for timber about 1953-54; footers remain in woods by the picnic area; gone.

facts.status_note: Taken down for timber around 1953-1954; the register says footers remain in the woods just north of the Big Bend picnic area

access.note: Picnic area reached by a side trip on FSR 206 (Scenic Drives USA); the tower site itself is not described as open or closed

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. The picnic area is reached by forest road FSR 206.

events.note: Built by the CCC on the Wythe Ranger District of the Jefferson National Forest, per the register (live-in cab with catwalk)
Purchased by Mr. Kime, creator of the Big Walker Lookout attraction on State Route 52, and dismantled for timber around 1953 to 1954
Coast and Geodetic Survey station described: mark just north of a picnic area at the old tower site, measured from the old tower's concrete footing
Appalachian Trail moved further north from its original route along the Walker Mountain ridge due to insufficient water sources
Registered October 30, 2010, nominated by Dan East (US 700, VA 5)

notes_for_editor: Gone status is confirmed by the Forest Fire Lookout Association county list. The 1941 CCC build year and the 20' cab rest on the register alone; '20' live-in cab' could mean the cab or the tower, so no height is recorded. Scenic Drives USA dates the picnic area to the 1930s, which is a different structure and is not used for the tower date. FSR 206 (Scenic Drives) and FS 206 (register) are treated as the same road; the story now says so. The register's footer description has no date. The register's account of footers is the only source for what remains. No staffing, fire, or design records found in these sources. Visit advice: no tower to climb; the picnic area is the only visit point described.
